title: WHOOP Brings Doctors Into Your Wrist This Summer
excerpt: Boston-based wearable giant launches on-demand clinician access and AI health tools for US members in summer 2026.
body:
WHOOP turned its fitness tracker into a clinical health platform on May 8, announcing live, on-demand video consultations with licensed clinicians for US members. The Boston-based company — valued at $10.1 billion after a $575 million funding round in March — is betting that continuous biometric data makes its telehealth offering fundamentally different from standalone virtual-doctor services.

**What WHOOP announced:**
Clinician consultations will launch in the United States this summer, embedded directly inside the WHOOP app. Unlike a typical telehealth visit, each session begins with months of the member's sleep, strain, and recovery data already visible to the clinician — plus bloodwork and medical history where available. WHOOP is also partnering with HealthEx to enable Electronic Health Record syncing, letting members pull diagnoses, medications, and procedures into the app in one secure step.

**The AI layer powering it:**
Alongside clinician access, WHOOP unveiled two AI features: *My Memory* and *Proactive Check-Ins*. My Memory lets members store and edit personal context so that AI coaching reflects real-world goals and circumstances. Proactive Check-Ins then surface timely, personalized nudges — adjusting training around travel or flagging sleep priorities before a big day — without requiring any manual input. Members can also now log habits, supplements, and life events by voice or text, with the AI suggesting what to track based on patterns it detects.

**What to watch:**
Live video consultations will carry an additional fee beyond the standard membership; exact pricing arrives when the feature goes live this summer, and how WHOOP navigates state-by-state telemedicine licensing rules will define how quickly it can scale.
nri_angle: Indian-Americans, who disproportionately carry risks for cardiovascular disease and diabetes yet often face gaps in preventive care access, stand to benefit directly from a wearable that now connects months of personalised biometric data to a licensed clinician on demand.
